newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy sees Mideast mission ending Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy sees Mideast mission ending Wednesday.

text.p: U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross said on Tuesday that he expected to continue his mission to try to restore Israeli-Palestinian security cooperation until Wednesday.

"I want to continue to follow up with discussions that have taken place so I will probably not leave tonight. I would guess I would leave tomorrow sometime," Ross told reporters after talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Ross arrived in the region at the weekend on a trip focused on security following a double suicide bombing by Moslem militants in Jerusalem that plunged Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking deep into crisis.

Tuesday's meeting was his third with Netanyahu, who accuses Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of doing "damn all" to crack down on militants in territory under his control. Ross was due to hold further talks with Arafat later on Tuesday.
The envoy said his mission, which could pave the way for a trip to the region by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, had a precise focus of restoring security cooperation.

He has already brought security experts from the two sides and from the United States together but cautioned that meetings alone were not enough. "We have a beginning, we have a step in the right direction but we need to see results," Ross said.
